context: In this work, we investigated various packing problems of orthogonal polygons under translation. For L-shapes, the yet smallest open case, we wondered whether they behave more like rectangles or convex polygons. For bin packing, we provided a surprisingly large lower bound on the competitive ratio of about n/log n for general L-shapes and n for general orthogonal polygons. That means that the trivial algorithm, which packs each item into its private bin, is worst-case optimal for orthogonal polygons. These lower bounds are much higher than for convex polygons, cf. Table 2. In contrast, for symmetric and small L-shapes there exist constant competitive algorithms. This insight implies that in terms of the competitive ratio, L-shapes behave more like rectangles for perimeter packing, area packing, and the online critical density. Many interesting problems remain for future work. Most notably, it remains to improve the bounds or even close the gaps for the problems stated in Tables 1 and 2. This includes the problem of determining the best competitive ratio for online bin packing of L-shapes, as it remains open whether it it possible to beat the trivial algorithm for L-BinPack.
